Manchester Planning Board Approves Revo Casino's Major Expansion

Published August 24, 2026 · 3 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

The Manchester, New Hampshire Planning Board has approved expansion plans for Revo Casino, clearing the way for the charitable gaming facility on South Willow Street to consolidate five separate parcels into a single 73,000-square-foot development anchored by new restaurants, a bar, entertainment stages, and a multipurpose event space.

What's changing on the site

The project, developed by the Granite State Poker Alliance alongside local developer Dick Anagnost, involves demolishing five existing structures on the consolidated site — a former bingo hall and movie theater, an EVEN Hotel, a Manchester Harley-Davidson dealership, a Taylor Rental location, and an Enterprise Car Sales building — to make way for the expanded gaming and entertainment complex. The plan calls for 1,086 parking spaces, including 22 ADA-accessible spots, well above the city's baseline requirement, along with landscaping that includes roughly 168 new trees and 679 new shrubs. A similar design for the site received its underlying variances and conditional site plan approval back in 2024; this week's Planning Board vote approves the specific lot-consolidation and phased-construction plan needed to move the project forward. Construction is expected to proceed in three phases — starting with demolition of the hotel, followed by the main build-out, and finishing with the transition of operations and remaining site infrastructure — designed to keep the existing casino operating with minimal disruption during the work.

Why it matters for New Hampshire players

New Hampshire permits charitable gaming facilities like Revo Casino to operate table games under a licensed-charity model rather than traditional commercial casino licensing, and Revo has become one of the state's larger gaming venues under that framework. A near-doubling of the property's footprint, with added dining, entertainment, and event space, signals continued investment in New Hampshire's gaming sector even as neighboring states dominate the region's broader casino and sports betting headlines. No opening date for the expanded facility has been set; the project will proceed in the phases outlined above once demolition begins.
